paraphrase: At Janaka's sacrifice Vidagdha Śākalya asked Yājñavalkya 'How many gods are there?' — three hundred and three and three thousand and three; then thirty-three; six; three; two; one and a half; one. The one god is the breath (prāṇa), called 'that' (tyad), Brahman. Śākalya, pressing further questions he could not answer, lost his head.

paraphrase: Brahman, the self-existent, practised austerity and considered: 'In austerity there is no infinity; come, let me offer myself in beings and beings in myself.' Having offered itself in all beings and all beings in itself, it attained supremacy, self-rule and sovereignty over all beings; so the sacrificer who performs the all-sacrifice (sarvamedha) attains the same.

paraphrase: The creatures came to Prajāpati for their ordinance. To the gods he said: sacrifice is your food, immortality your strength, the sun your light. To the ancestors, who came with the sacred cord over the right shoulder: monthly shall be your food, svadhā your drink, the moon your light. To men: evening and morning your food, offspring your death, fire your light. To the beasts: eat whenever you find; and to the Asuras he gave darkness and magic (māyā).
